purpose: Lets a user enter a short piece of free-form text. It is the primary control for collecting typed data such as names, email addresses, search terms, and passwords. For multi-line text, use a Textarea instead.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label for the field. Always required — a field without a label is inaccessible.

props.name: type
props.description: The HTML input type. Controls the keyboard on mobile and the browser's built-in validation.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hint text shown when the field is empty. Use sparingly — it disappears on input and must not replace a label.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: When set, puts the field into an error state and displays this message below the input. Must explain what went wrong and how to fix it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field. Prefer hiding it or explaining why it is unavailable.

variants.name: default
variants.whenToUse: Any time the user needs to type a short piece of text. This is the standard form field.

variants.name: error
variants.whenToUse: After the user has submitted or left the field and the value fails validation. Always pair with an errorMessage that says what went wrong.

states.name: default
states.description: Resting state. Neutral border, white background.

states.name: focus
states.description: Keyboard or pointer focus. Border and outline shift to the focus-ring token.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Non-interactive. Uses disabled surface and text tokens, not-allowed cursor.

states.name: error
states.description: Validation has failed. Border and message use the error token. aria-invalid is set.

antiPatterns.never: Omit the label prop or replace it with only a placeholder.
antiPatterns.because: A placeholder disappears the moment the user starts typing, leaving them with no way to recall what the field asked for. Screen readers announce the label, not the placeholder. A field without a label is inaccessible.

antiPatterns.never: Show an error state before the user has had a chance to interact with the field.
antiPatterns.because: Pre-emptive errors feel punishing and create anxiety. Validation should fire on blur or submit, not on mount.

antiPatterns.never: Set raw colour or spacing values on the input.
antiPatterns.because: Unbound values are invisible to the design system and to an agent reading it. Always bind to a token.

antiPatterns.never: Use an Input for multi-line text entry.
antiPatterns.because: A single-line input clips long text and sets the wrong expectation. Use a Textarea for anything that might be more than one line.

keyboard: Tab moves focus into the field
Enter may submit the enclosing form
accessibility.focus: Native focus order. Visible 2px focus ring on :focus-visible using the focus-ring token, offset by 2px. Focus ring colour shifts to error token when in error state.
aria: aria-describedby points to the error message element when errorMessage is set
label is always associated via htmlFor/id — never use aria-label as a substitute for a visible label
accessibility.contrast: Error red on white meets WCAG AA 4.5:1. Disabled text on disabled surface meets WCAG AA 4.5:1 for the default token set.

examples: Please enter a valid email address.

agentNotes: Always pass a label that names the data being collected, not the action ('Email address', not 'Enter email'). When building a form, pair each Input with a Button for submission. Never generate a form where the only label context is inside the placeholder.
